name: PalmSense curated palmistry knowledge base
sources: Cheiro (William John Warner), 'Cheiro's Language of the Hand' (1897, public domain)
General traditional palmistry conventions, summarised and rewritten in our own words by the project team

entries.text: In traditional palmistry a long heart line is associated with an open, generous and expressive emotional nature.
A short heart line is traditionally read as a more private person who shows affection through actions rather than words.
A heart line that curves upward toward the fingers is classically linked with warmth, romance and openly showing feelings.

entries.condition: runs fairly straight across the palm
entries.text: A heart line running straight across the palm is traditionally linked with a calm, rational approach to emotions.
A deep, clearly marked heart line is said in palmistry to suggest strong and steady emotional commitment.
A faint heart line is traditionally read as sensitivity and a tendency to keep emotions guarded.
A curved heart line is described in palmistry as an affectionate, spontaneous temperament.
A straight heart line is often described as practical and thoughtful in matters of the heart.
When the heart line cannot be seen clearly in the photo, no traditional reading of it should be given.
A long head line is traditionally linked with thorough thinking, planning and enjoyment of detailed work.
A short head line is classically read as quick, decisive and practical thinking.
A straight head line is associated in palmistry with logical, analytical and structured thinking - often linked with technical or business careers.
A head line sloping toward the wrist is traditionally linked with imagination and creativity, often associated with artistic or creative careers.
A curved head line is said to show flexible, creative thinking.
A deep head line is traditionally read as strong concentration and a focused mind.
A faint head line is traditionally read as a mind that prefers variety and may wander between ideas.
When the head and life lines start joined together, palmistry traditionally describes a careful person who thinks before acting.
When the head line starts separately from the life line, tradition describes an independent, adventurous spirit.
When the head line is not clearly visible, palmistry readings about thinking style should not be given.
In palmistry a long life line is read as vitality and enthusiasm. It does NOT predict how long a person will live.
A short life line is a common feature; palmists say it does NOT mean a short life - it is traditionally read as independence.
A life line making a wide arc into the palm is traditionally linked with energy, enthusiasm and love of activity.
A life line hugging the thumb is traditionally read as a reserved, home-loving and cautious nature.
A deep, clear life line is traditionally associated with a stable, energetic life path.
A faint life line is traditionally read as a gentle or variable energy level; it is not a health prediction.
A strongly curved life line is classically associated with stamina and a warm, outgoing nature.
If the life line is unclear, no reading of it should be given, and it must never be connected to health or lifespan.
A visible fate line is traditionally linked with a sense of direction and a career path shaped by personal goals.
A long fate line is read in palmistry as steady commitment to one career direction.
A shorter fate line is traditionally read as a career direction that becomes clear later in life.
Many people have no visible fate line. Palmists traditionally read this as a flexible, self-made path with many possible directions.
A straight fate line is traditionally linked with a consistent, well-planned career.
An Earth hand (square palm, shorter fingers) is traditionally described as practical, reliable and hard-working.
Earth hands are traditionally linked with hands-on careers such as engineering, farming, building or management.
An Air hand (square palm, long fingers) is traditionally described as curious, communicative and intellectual.
Air hands are traditionally linked with communication, teaching, writing, IT and analytical careers.
A Water hand (long palm, long fingers) is traditionally described as sensitive, intuitive and imaginative.
Water hands are traditionally linked with creative, caring and artistic careers.
A Fire hand (long palm, shorter fingers) is traditionally described as energetic, confident and enthusiastic.
Fire hands are traditionally linked with leadership, entrepreneurship, sports and performance.
Traditional palmistry links a strong, long head line with careful planning, which palmists connect with steady management of money.
A clear fate line is traditionally connected with financial stability coming from consistent work.
Earth hands are traditionally associated with saving and practical, cautious money habits.
Fire and Air hands are traditionally associated with opportunity-seeking and new ventures.
Palmistry has no scientific ability to predict wealth. Any prosperity theme is a traditional story only and must not guide financial decisions.
A common palmistry tradition says the non-dominant hand shows natural potential and the dominant hand shows what a person has developed.
When both palms look similar, palmists traditionally say a person has stayed close to their natural tendencies.
Palmistry is a cultural and entertainment practice. It is not scientifically validated for predicting personality, health, wealth, relationships or the future.
Palm lines must never be used to make health or lifespan predictions. For health questions, consult a medical professional.
Many fine creases are traditionally read as a sensitive, detail-aware personality.
A palm with few extra creases is traditionally read as a calm, uncomplicated temperament.
